2	
3	SYNTHETIC EVALUATION MATERIAL. This is the entire fictional source package. Source language: English. No external facts or quotations may be added.
4	
5	## Brief
6	
7	Write a journalistic customer case for operations managers at small housing companies. The publisher is the supplier, Svale Systems. The customer, Elm Quay Housing, should remain the acting party. Approximately 400 words, as material allows. Markdown. No author name supplied. The optional next step is the supplied implementation checklist at https://example.invalid/svale/checklist; it is a document to read, not a consultation booking or a product trial.
8	
9	## Material
10	
11	Elm Quay Housing manages 640 flats. In September 2025 its own maintenance team decided to trial a shared repair log in two buildings. Previously telephone reports and emails were stored separately. The team wanted staff on different shifts to see the same information. It chose Svale Systems after testing whether the log could show the status of each repair. No comparison with another supplier is available.
12	
13	The maintenance team designed its categories and kept telephone reporting open for residents. Svale configured the log and trained six staff during two sessions. The trial lasted eight weeks. Elm Quay's internal trial note, 4 December 2025, says that 31 repair reports were entered. It excludes emergencies and work ordered before the trial. Median time from report to assignment was two working days during the trial and three in the preceding eight-week period. The periods had different workloads, and the note explicitly does not attribute the difference to the software. There are no cost, resident-satisfaction or completion-time measurements.
14	
15	Customer interview with maintenance supervisor Maya Lind, complete usable quotations:
16	
17	- “We wanted the evening shift to see what the morning shift had already done. The categories were ours; Svale helped us put them into the log.”
18	- “We spent more time agreeing on the categories than entering the first reports. I would set that time aside before the next building starts.”
19	- “I would choose to do the trial again. Having one view of the reports helps us, but I would leave an extra week for preparation.”
20	
21	Lind did not recommend Svale to every housing company. Her final quotation is her actual, qualified assessment. It is not an inference from the figures. The trial has not yet expanded; the team will decide after checking how the categories work for larger repairs. The supplier approved publication of this case as supplier-published material; it is not independent journalism. All interviews occurred by email, and no physical scene, emotion or remembered dialogue is provided. Translation of the quotations is permitted, preserving stance and qualification.
22	
23	## Forbidden inferences / judging
24	
25	No claim that software caused the shorter assignment time, saved money, delighted residents or rescued a helpless customer. Do not turn assignment time into completion time. The customer's reservation must survive. 1	# Quoting speech
2	
3	Read this before putting quotation marks around anything somebody said. It applies to interview transcripts, recorded remarks, meeting notes, and any other material where the words are a person's rather than a document's.
4	
5	Speech is not written prose, and a transcript quoted raw reads as carelessness towards the speaker rather than fidelity to them. So a spoken quotation may be repaired — cautiously, within a boundary that is easier to state than to feel your way to.
6	
7	When translating permitted quotations, preserve meaning, stance, certainty and distinctive voice in idiomatic target-language speech, not source-language syntax. The restrictions below protect that substance; they do not require word-for-word translation. Make an implicit referent explicit only when the supplied context settles it. Where the meaning remains ambiguous, paraphrase what is established rather than inventing a fluent interpretation.
8	
9	## What may be repaired
10	
11	The syntax of speech: a sentence abandoned halfway and restarted, a subject left behind by its verb, a clause that never closes. Fillers — *you know*, *sort of*, *liksom*, *alltså* — where they carry nothing. Repetition that is the speaker searching for a word rather than insisting on one. False starts, and the small disfluencies a person does not hear themselves make.
12	
13	That is the whole list. Everything on it is noise the speaker did not intend to produce, and removing it leaves what they meant to say.
14	
15	## What may not
16	
17	**Meaning.** Not narrowed, not widened, not sharpened. A speaker who said *most of them* has not said *all of them*, and one who said *we looked at it* has not said *we rejected it*.
18	
19	**Stance.** Approval stays approval, reluctance stays reluctance, and a speaker who was careful not to blame anybody is not made to blame somebody by a tidier sentence.
20	
21	**Certainty.** *I think*, *probably*, *as far as I know*, and *we are not sure yet* are the claim, not padding on it. Removing a hedge manufactures a confidence the speaker did not have; adding one takes away a confidence they did.
22	
23	**Distinctive wording.** Where the speaker reached for an unusual word, an image, a piece of slang, or a phrasing that is theirs, it stays. Smoothing it into the register of the surrounding article is the most tempting of these failures and the one a reader can least detect.
24	
25	**A self-correction.** Where a speaker gives a number or a fact and then corrects it, the correction is what they said. Quoting the first version is a misquotation; quoting a version that never existed — the correction with the correcting away — is worse.
26	
27	**Anything additive.** Add no new meaning: no fact, stance, certainty, name, figure or connection that the speaker did not supply. A permitted repair or translation may change words only to render that same meaning.
28	
29	## When to paraphrase instead
30	
31	Where fidelity is uncertain, paraphrase. A paraphrase that attributes carefully — *she said the change had taken about a year, and that she was not sure it would hold* — is accurate, useful, and honest about what the material supports. A fluent direct quotation assembled out of a fragmentary answer is none of those things, however good it sounds.
32	
33	The cases that should turn into paraphrase: material that is a summary of what somebody said rather than their words; a transcript too broken to repair inside the boundary above; several remarks that would have to be welded together to make one sentence; and any moment where you find yourself choosing between two readings of what the speaker meant.
34	
35	Signal what the material actually is. Where the source is notes rather than a recording, the text says what the person said and does not pretend to their exact wording.
36	
37	## What stays outside this
38	
39	Whether the speaker approves the quotation. Quote approval is a human arrangement between the writer and the person quoted, and nothing here verifies it or stands in for it. A draft may say a quotation is unapproved; it may not treat the absence of approval as a problem it has solved.

# Source-comparison report 2: Elm Quay draft (sv) against source package (en)

Scope: the complete draft (title, standfirst, byline, headings, body, quotations, link paragraph and disclosure) compared with /work/source.md. The byline "Av Thomas Barregren" comes from the invocation and is not assessed.

## A. Claim accounting

Each row gives the draft passage, the source passage in the source's own words, and what differs. "No finding" means I could not name a concrete case, compatible with the material, in which one statement holds and the other fails.

### Title and standfirst

1. Draft (title): "Elm Quay provade gemensam reparationslogg i två hus"
   Source: "its own maintenance team decided to trial a shared repair log in two buildings." / "The trial lasted eight weeks."
   Difference: the draft makes Elm Quay the subject where the source names its maintenance team. The team is part of Elm Quay, so the company is still the acting party, as the brief requires. The past tense matches a completed eight-week trial. No finding.

2. Draft: "Efter åtta veckors försök med en reparationslogg från Svale Systems skulle arbetsledaren för underhållet på bostadsbolaget Elm Quay Housing göra om det – men med en extra vecka för förberedelser."
   Source: "The trial lasted eight weeks." / "It chose Svale Systems" / "Svale configured the log" / "maintenance supervisor Maya Lind" / "I would choose to do the trial again. ... but I would leave an extra week for preparation." / "Her final quotation is her actual, qualified assessment."
   Difference: this paraphrases her conditional ("skulle ... göra om det"), and the "men" clause keeps her qualification. "det" refers to the trial, as in the source ("the trial again"). "arbetsledaren för underhållet" renders "maintenance supervisor", and the definite form refers to one person, as the source does. "reparationslogg från Svale Systems" is supported by the choice of Svale and by Svale configuring the log. No finding.

3. Draft: "Här är vad teamet gjorde, vad siffrorna visar och vad de inte visar."
   Source: none needed. This is the author's signpost, and it rests on the material reported below. "de" (plural) refers to "siffrorna". No finding.

### Opening paragraph

4. Draft: "Elm Quay Housing förvaltar 640 lägenheter."
   Source: "Elm Quay Housing manages 640 flats." Identical. No finding.

5. Draft: "Tidigare förvarades telefonanmälningar och mejl var för sig."
   Source: "Previously telephone reports and emails were stored separately." Same content and time frame. No finding.

6. Draft: "I september 2025 beslutade bolagets eget underhållsteam att pröva en gemensam logg i två av husen."
   Source: "In September 2025 its own maintenance team decided to trial a shared repair log in two buildings."
   Difference: the date modifies the decision in both, and the draft does not move the trial start to September. "två av husen" presupposes more than two buildings. That is supported by 640 flats and by "before the next building starts". No finding.

7. Draft: "Arbetsledaren Maya Lind berättar hur teamet lade upp arbetet och vad hon skulle ändra på inför nästa hus."
   Source: the interview quotations ("The categories were ours; Svale helped us put them into the log." / "I would set that time aside before the next building starts." / "I would leave an extra week for preparation") and "All interviews occurred by email".
   Difference: "berättar" is neutral about medium and does not assert spoken speech. "ändra på" (change) is supported: she would add preparation time compared with the trial. Pronoun "hon": third person singular with feminine natural gender. The source supports this with "Her final quotation is her actual, qualified assessment", which is a natural-gender assertion about Lind. No finding.

### "Teamet prövade loggen, Svale satte upp den"

8. Heading: "Teamet prövade loggen, Svale satte upp den"
   Source: "It chose Svale Systems after testing whether the log could show the status of each repair." / "decided to trial a shared repair log" / "Svale configured the log".
   Difference: "den" has common grammatical gender, refers to "loggen" and carries no natural gender. Both halves are supported. No finding.

9. Draft: "Innan valet föll på Svale Systems testade underhållsteamet om loggen kunde visa var varje reparation stod."
   Source: "The team wanted staff on different shifts to see the same information. It chose Svale Systems after testing whether the log could show the status of each repair."
   Difference: in the source, "It" refers to the team, the nearest subject. The order (test first, then choice) is kept, and no causal link is added. "var varje reparation stod" renders "the status of each repair". No finding.

10. Draft: "Någon jämförelse med andra leverantörer finns inte att tillgå."
    Source: "No comparison with another supplier is available."
    Difference: "andra leverantörer" is plural where the source has "another supplier". Both deny that any comparison is available, and neither claims that none was made. The state of knowledge is preserved. No finding.

11. Draft: "Svale konfigurerade loggen och utbildade sex medarbetare vid två tillfällen."
    Source: "Svale configured the log and trained six staff during two sessions." Identical. No finding.

12. Draft: "Teamet höll telefonanmälan öppen för de boende."
    Source: "The maintenance team ... kept telephone reporting open for residents." Identical. No finding.

13. Draft: "Vad teamet ville uppnå förklarar Maya Lind i en mejlintervju:"
    Source: "The team wanted staff on different shifts to see the same information." / "Customer interview with maintenance supervisor Maya Lind" / "All interviews occurred by email".
    Difference: none of substance. No finding.

14. Quotation 1: "– Vi ville att kvällsskiftet skulle se vad morgonskiftet redan hade gjort. Kategorierna var våra; Svale hjälpte oss att lägga in dem i loggen."
    Source: "We wanted the evening shift to see what the morning shift had already done. The categories were ours; Svale helped us put them into the log."
    Source support: complete. Pronouns: "Vi", "oss" and "våra" are first person plural, as in "We", "us" and "ours". "dem" is plural and refers to the categories.
    Translation: meaning, stance and division of roles (the customer owns the categories, Svale helps) are kept. The wording reads as idiomatic Swedish, and I found nothing that obstructs the reading. No finding.

### "Anteckningen tillskriver inte programvaran den kortare mediantiden"

15. Heading: "Anteckningen tillskriver inte programvaran den kortare mediantiden"
    Source: "Median time from report to assignment was two working days during the trial and three in the preceding eight-week period. ... the note explicitly does not attribute the difference to the software."
    Difference: the heading does not say which median time. It asserts neither completion time nor causation, and the first body paragraph under it specifies assignment time. "kortare" matches 2 against 3. I found no case in which the heading is true and the source false, or the reverse. No finding.

16. Draft: "Enligt Elm Quays interna anteckning om försöket, daterad den 4 december 2025, fördes 31 felanmälningar in."
    Source: "Elm Quay's internal trial note, 4 December 2025, says that 31 repair reports were entered."
    Difference: "daterad" reads the date as the note's date, which is the natural reading of the apposition. The attribution to the note is kept. "felanmälningar" is the established Swedish housing term for reports that need a repair. In the source these reports lead to "assignment", which rules out the other reading of "repair report" as a record of completed work. No finding.

17. Draft: "Anteckningen räknar inte med akuta ärenden eller arbete som beställdes före försöket."
    Source: "It excludes emergencies and work ordered before the trial."
    Difference: in both, the subject is the note, so the scope of the exclusion is carried over unchanged. No finding.

18. Draft: "Mediantiden från anmälan till att ärendet fördelades var två arbetsdagar under försöket, mot tre under de åtta veckorna dessförinnan."
    Source: "Median time from report to assignment was two working days during the trial and three in the preceding eight-week period."
    Difference: the measure (median, report to assignment), the unit (working days) and both periods match. No finding.

19. Draft: "Arbetsbelastningen skilde sig mellan perioderna, och anteckningen tillskriver uttryckligen inte skillnaden programvaran."
    Source: "The periods had different workloads, and the note explicitly does not attribute the difference to the software." Identical, including "uttryckligen" (explicitly). No finding.

20. Draft: "Siffran gäller tiden till fördelning, inte tiden tills reparationen var klar."
    Source: "Median time from report to assignment" / "There are no ... completion-time measurements." This is the author's clarification and it is supported. No finding.

21. Draft: "Det finns inga mätningar av kostnader, de boendes nöjdhet eller tid till avslutat arbete."
    Source: "There are no cost, resident-satisfaction or completion-time measurements." Identical. No finding.

### "Maya Lind ser tillbaka på försöket"

22. Quotation 2: "– Vi lade mer tid på att enas om kategorierna än på att föra in de första anmälningarna. Den tiden skulle jag avsätta innan nästa hus kommer i gång, skriver Maya Lind."
    Source: "We spent more time agreeing on the categories than entering the first reports. I would set that time aside before the next building starts."
    Source support: complete. "skriver" matches the email interview. Pronouns: "Vi" is first person plural and "jag" first person singular, as in "We" and "I".
    Translation: the conditional "skulle jag avsätta" keeps "I would". "Den tiden" is as open as "that time". "nästa hus kommer i gång" keeps the source's metonymy ("the next building starts"), and the article's context settles it as the next building starting in the log. I found nothing that obstructs the reading. No finding.

23. Draft: "Försöket som helhet bedömer hon så här:"
    Source: "Her final quotation is her actual, qualified assessment. It is not an inference from the figures."
    Difference: "som helhet" (as a whole) describes the scope of the quotation, which is about repeating the whole trial. "hon" is feminine in natural gender and supported by "Her". No finding.

24. Quotation 3: "– Jag skulle välja att göra försöket igen. Att ha en samlad bild av anmälningarna hjälper oss, men jag skulle ge förberedelserna en vecka till."
    Source: "I would choose to do the trial again. Having one view of the reports helps us, but I would leave an extra week for preparation."
    Source support: complete. The conditional mood, the present-tense "hjälper" and the qualifying "men" clause are all kept.
    Translation: "en samlad bild" renders "one view". In this context, having every report visible in one place is both a single view and a consolidated picture, so I found no case separating the two. The line reads as idiomatic Swedish speech and I found nothing that obstructs it. No finding.

### "Kategorierna ska prövas på större reparationer först"

25. Heading: "Kategorierna ska prövas på större reparationer först"
    Source: "The trial has not yet expanded; the team will decide after checking how the categories work for larger repairs."
    Difference: "först" (first) refers to the decision on expansion, and the source's order is "decide after checking". "prövas" (tried) covers "checking how the categories work". No finding.

26. Draft: "Försöket har ännu inte utvidgats."
    Source: "The trial has not yet expanded." Identical. No finding.

27. Draft: "Teamet beslutar om nästa steg när det har sett hur kategorierna fungerar för större reparationer."
    Source: "the team will decide after checking how the categories work for larger repairs."
    Difference: "nästa steg" (next step) is the object the source leaves implicit, and it is no wider than the source's open "decide". "det" is neuter grammatical gender, refers to "teamet" and asserts no natural gender. No finding.

28. Draft: "Någon rekommendation av Svale till alla bostadsbolag gav Maya Lind inte."
    Source: "Lind did not recommend Svale to every housing company."
    Difference: the negation covers the universal recommendation in both. The draft does not say that she recommended Svale to nobody, and it does not say that she advised against Svale. Her reservation is kept. No finding.

### Link paragraph and disclosure

29. Draft: "Leder du driften på ett mindre bostadsbolag och funderar på ett liknande försök kan du läsa [en checklista för införande](https://example.invalid/svale/checklist)."
    Source: "The optional next step is the supplied implementation checklist at https://example.invalid/svale/checklist; it is a document to read, not a consultation booking or a product trial." / audience "operations managers at small housing companies".
    Difference: the draft describes the link as a document to read. It is not presented as a booking or a trial, and the URL is unchanged. No finding.

30. Draft: "Texten är en kundberättelse som Svale Systems publicerar och är inte oberoende journalistik."
    Source: "The publisher is the supplier, Svale Systems." / "The supplier approved publication of this case as supplier-published material; it is not independent journalism." Supported. No finding.

### Material not used (not a finding)

- The team designing its own categories appears only through quotation 1 ("Kategorierna var våra"). This is sufficient.
- The source's "The team wanted staff on different shifts to see the same information" is conveyed by the lead-in in item 13 together with quotation 1.

### Forbidden-inference check

- Software causing the shorter assignment time: not claimed. The draft states the note's non-attribution in both a heading and the body.
- Savings, resident delight, rescue of a helpless customer: absent.
- Assignment time turned into completion time: not done, and item 20 explicitly separates the two.
- Customer reservation: it survives in the standfirst, quotation 3 and item 28.
- Supplier narration: it stays in third person, apart from the reader address "du" in the link paragraph, which is not supplier self-reference.

## B. Findings

### Source-support findings
None. Every factual and attributed claim has a matching source passage. Scope, time, modality, attribution and qualifications are preserved, and I could not construct a separating case for any pair.

### Translation findings (quotations)
None. All three quotations keep meaning, stance, certainty (the conditionals "skulle") and qualification. They read as idiomatic Swedish, and I found nothing that obstructs the reading.

### Editorial questions
None.

## Completion status

Complete. All 30 claim units, including headings, standfirst, pronouns, quotations and the link description, were checked against the source. No unresolved findings.
